title: St. Joe Foundation donated over $100k to two FSU Panama City campus programs - NewsBreak
text:
PANAMA CITY, Fla. ( WMBB ) – FSU Panama City is expecting to welcome more students this fall, and they just got a boost of support to make it happen. On Wednesday morning, the St. Joe Foundation presented the University’s Collegiate School and early childhood autism program with a donation of over $100,000. ECAP, which helps students with autism and other developmental disabilities, is receiving nearly three-quarters of this donation. That will help them continue their scholarship program, which helps serve over 40 local families. “We have a clinic here on campus that kids get to come to because of partners like St Joe Foundation at no cost to their family,” Associate Dean of Academic Affairs & ECAP Development Director Dr. Amy Polick said. That clinic includes their new independent living and learning center, which helps students learn skills like cooking, making the bed, and other household tasks. Over at the collegiate school, they’re getting nearly $40,000 for furnishing a facility meant to hold high schoolers who haven’t graduated but are already taking college courses full-time. “Most of those students, by the end of their 11th grade, will have their associate’s and arts degree. So, since those students are fully on campus here in Panama City, we need space for them,” FSU PC Collegiate School Director Debbi Whitaker said. Both student populations will occupy the two floors of the school’s technology building.
With the new funding and the proximity, the opportunities for joint learning are endless. “We look forward to having those types of collaborations, including student-to-student interactions,” Whitaker added.
